## Appearance

Anne is a thin girl with a slim milk-white throat, long thin legs, and a pointed freckled face featuring solemn gray eyes. Over time, her face brightens with delicate features and starrier eyes, while her cheeks carry a faint flush and her skin becomes less freckled than it used to be. Known for her bright-eyed and animated demeanor, she eventually grows taller than [Aunt Josephine](../character/josephine-barry.md). Her notable hair, which has streamed behind her in a torrent of brightness, includes long red braids, though at one point it was shingled short after turning green, and later appears as a ruddy, auburn, or splendid [Titian](../character/titian.md) shade.

## Personality

Driven by strong academic ambitions, this highly imaginative individual strives to pass her examinations at the head of the list, become a teacher, and win the Avery scholarship to study at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college). She is particularly motivated to excel in her studies to make [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) proud, though her vivid imagination sometimes leads to forgetfulness regarding her daily duties. Additionally, she harbors a deep dread of passing through the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P20](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0020), [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P9](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XX. ## History

Born in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Anne Shirley grew up as an orphan, raised initially by Mrs. [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md) until age eight—caring for four younger children—and later by Mrs. [Hammond](../character/hammond.md) before spending four months at an asylum in [Hopeton](../codex/places.md#hopeton). Adopted by mistake instead of a boy, she is brought to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) by [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), where his sister [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) initially intends to return her to Mrs. [Spencer](../character/spencer.md). Upon realizing Anne might be placed with the harsh Mrs. [Blewett](../character/peter-blewett.md), [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) decides to keep her. Despite causing early tension by exploding at Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) over her red hair, Anne delivers a dramatic apology to restore peace. She forms an immediate bond with [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), solemnizing their friendship in the garden, though their bond is briefly severed when Anne accidentally gets [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) drunk on currant wine. After Anne saves Diana's younger sister from croup during a winter medical crisis, Mrs. [Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) permits the girls to resume their friendship.

## Quotes

> "You would cry, too, if you were an orphan and had come to a place you thought was going to be home and found that they didn’t want you because you weren’t a boy. Oh, this is the most tragical thing that ever happened to me!"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P11](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0011)

> "but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P19](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0019)

> "why didn’t you tell me at the station that you didn’t want me and leave me there? If I hadn’t seen the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters it wouldn’t be so hard."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P25](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0025)

> "She brought Lily Jones for herself. Lily is only five years old and she is very beautiful and had nut-brown hair. If I was very beautiful and had nut-brown hair would you keep me?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0029)

> "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P24](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0024)

## Relationships

### [Allan](../character/allan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/allan--anne-shirley.md)

Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md) is Avonlea's minister's wife and Anne's beloved Sunday school teacher. Anne falls in love with her immediately and eagerly hosts her for tea, though the occasion is briefly ruined when Anne accidentally bakes a cake flavored with liniment. Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md) handles the mishap with kindness, comforting Anne and later hosting her at the manse for a wonderful afternoon.

- Friend of — minister's wife and confidante  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024)</sub>

### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

[Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) is Anne's dearest friend and self-described 'bosom friend.' Their bond began with a dramatic oath of friendship in the garden, and they spend their time walking together, sharing imaginative games, and exchanging notes. Despite a temporary separation imposed by Diana's mother after Anne accidentally served [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) wine, their close companionship is restored after Anne saves Diana's younger sister.
